mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months signals contraction in manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings for industrial firms and drags down S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during four consecutive months of INDPRO decline.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) for two consecutive months indicates a broad-based weakening in demand, which depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both GDPC1 and HOUST decline for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is below 1% and CPI inflation rises above 2% for three consecutive months, the central bank is likely to signal or implement monetary tightening, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1% AND CPIAUCSL > 2% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when FEDFUNDS < 1% and CPIAUCSL > 2% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above 0.5% month-over-month for two consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 0.5% MoM for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS increases by more than 0.5% MoM for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A strong positive correlation between real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and industrial production (INDPRO) over a six-month window indicates synchronized demand and supply expansion, which supports higher corporate earnings and results in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: Positive correlation between GDPC1 and INDPRO over six months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when GDPC1 and INDPRO are positively correlated over a six-month window.
